```{r}
#| label: setup
pacman::p_load(sf, tmap, tidyverse, knitr)
sf_use_s2(FALSE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(out.width = "100%", dpi = 150, dev.args = list(bg = "transparent"))

prep   <- read_rds("data/rds/prepared.rds")
lmsa   <- read_rds("data/rds/results_lmsa.rds")
ehsa   <- read_rds("data/rds/results_ehsa.rds")
bonus  <- read_rds("data/rds/results_bonus.rds")
regs   <- read_rds("data/rds/results_regions.rds")
charts <- read_rds("data/rds/charts.rds")

mmr <- prep$mmr_conflict
mmr_st <- mmr %>% group_by(ST) %>% summarise()
nudge <- tribble(~ST, ~dx_km, ~dy_km,
  "Ayeyarwady", -45, -15, "Yangon", 15, -40, "Mon", -15, -45, "Bago (West)", -35, 25, "Bago (East)", 30, -15,
  "Kayin", 45, 10, "Shan (South)", -25, 0, "Shan (East)", 40, 0, "Tanintharyi", 80, 0)
st_lab <- st_point_on_surface(mmr_st) %>%
  mutate(x = st_coordinates(.)[, 1], y = st_coordinates(.)[, 2]) %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>% left_join(nudge, by = "ST") %>%
  mutate(x = x + coalesce(dx_km, 0) * 1000, y = y + coalesce(dy_km, 0) * 1000) %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("x", "y"), crs = st_crs(mmr_st))
tmap_options(scale = 1.3, component.autoscale = FALSE)
dz <- c("Sagaing", "Magway", "Mandalay")

col_high <- "#D55E00"; col_low <- "#0072B2"; col_hl <- "#E69F00"; col_lh <- "#56B4E9"; col_ns <- "#EDE8DF"
bg <- "#FDFAF3"
ehsa_cols <- c("New hotspot" = "#7A0177", "Consecutive hotspot" = "#67001F", "Intensifying hotspot" = "#B2182B",
               "Persistent hotspot" = "#3F0011", "Diminishing hotspot" = "#FDDBC7", "Oscillating hotspot" = "#E66101",
               "Sporadic hotspot" = "#FDB863", "Historical hotspot" = "#FDD0A2",
               "New coldspot" = "#542788", "Consecutive coldspot" = "#2166AC", "Intensifying coldspot" = "#053061",
               "Persistent coldspot" = "#08306B", "Diminishing coldspot" = "#D1E5F0", "Oscillating coldspot" = "#4393C3",
               "Sporadic coldspot" = "#92C5DE", "Historical coldspot" = "#C6DBEF",
               "No pattern detected" = "#A8A8A8", "Not significant" = col_ns)
ehsa_levels <- names(ehsa_cols)

map_layout <- tm_layout(bg.color = bg, outer.bg.color = bg, frame = FALSE, legend.bg.color = bg,
                        inner.margins = c(0.01, 0.01, 0.01, 0.01), outer.margins = 0)
name_box <- function(st) tm_shape(filter(st_lab, ST %in% st)) +
  tm_text("ST", size = 0.75, col = "grey5", bgcol = "white", bgcol_alpha = 0.7)
states <- tm_shape(mmr_st) + tm_borders(col = "grey25", lwd = 0.7)

theme_slide <- theme_minimal(base_size = 18) +
  theme(plot.title = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
        plot.background = element_rect(fill = bg, colour = NA),
        panel.background = element_rect(fill = bg, colour = NA))

n_events <- sum(mmr$total)
dz_share <- sum(mmr$total[mmr$ST %in% dz]) / n_events
hq <- lmsa$hcsa %>% st_drop_geometry() %>% mutate(hot = str_detect(spot, "Hot"), cold = str_detect(spot, "Cold"))
lq <- lmsa$lisa %>% st_drop_geometry()
et <- ehsa$ehsa_tab %>% left_join(st_drop_geometry(mmr) %>% select(TS_PCODE, TS, ST), by = "TS_PCODE")
tot <- et %>% filter(variable == "All armed conflict"); sig_tot <- tot %>% filter(p_value < 0.05)
np <- function(p, v = "All armed conflict", s = NULL) sum(et$variable == v & et$p_value < 0.05 & et$pattern == p & (is.null(s) | et$ST %in% s))
rm_n <- function(y, w) charts$remote_mix$n[charts$remote_mix$year == y & charts$remote_mix$weapon == w]
air_x <- rm_n("2024", "Military air strike") / rm_n("2021", "Military air strike")
q_tot <- charts$trend %>% group_by(quarter) %>% summarise(n = sum(n)); peak <- slice_max(q_tot, n, n = 1)
gq <- bonus$geary
urban <- gq %>% filter(profile == "Few battles, more bombs or attacks on civilians")
core <- lq %>% filter(quadrant == "High-High", ST == "Sagaing") %>% pull(TS_PCODE)
core_q <- range(tot$hot_q[tot$TS_PCODE %in% core])

html_legend <- function(cols, present) {
  keep <- cols[names(cols) %in% present]
  paste0(sprintf('<span><i style="color:%s">&#9632;</i> %s</span>', keep, names(keep)), collapse = " ")
}
shown_levels <- function(v) {
  x <- ehsa_sf(v)$shown
  levels(droplevels(x))
}

ehsa_sf <- function(v) mmr %>% select(TS_PCODE) %>%
  left_join(et %>% filter(variable %in% v), by = "TS_PCODE") %>%
  mutate(shown = factor(if_else(p_value < 0.05, pattern, "Not significant"), levels = ehsa_levels))
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 5

                labels = c("0", "1 to 25", "26 to 100", "101 to 250", "251 to 500", "501 or more"),
                values = "brewer.oranges"),

```
:::

::: {.column width="55%"}
<div class="kicker">Research question</div>

<div class="rq">Where does armed conflict in Myanmar cluster, and how have these clusters changed since the 2021 coup?</div>

<div class="statrow">
<div><div class="bignum">`r format(n_events, big.mark = ",")`</div><div class="bigcap">armed conflict events, January 2021 to September 2025</div></div>
<div><div class="bignum">`r format(peak$n, big.mark = ",")`</div><div class="bigcap">events in `r peak$quarter`, the peak, as Operation 1027 began</div></div>
</div>

<div class="fix"><b>Study area.</b> All 330 townships of Myanmar. Black outline, the Dry Zone of Sagaing, Magway and Mandalay.</div>

<div class="fix"><b>Data.</b> ACLED events (battles, explosions and remote violence, violence against civilians) and MIMU township boundaries, counted by township and quarter.</div>
:::
:::::

::: notes
Since the coup ACLED has recorded about 54,000 armed conflict events in Myanmar. They are far from even. The Dry Zone, outlined in black, holds 43 percent of them. The study asks where conflict clusters and how those clusters have changed, which is what anyone planning aid, protection or peace-keeping needs to know.
:::

## Clear the data land mines, then test every map against chance {.approach}

<div class="part">Part 1 · The question and the data</div>

::::: columns
::: {.column width="46%"}
<div class="kicker">Three land mines that would have misled the analysis</div>

<div class="fix"><b>6 rows were not in Myanmar.</b> Incidents off India and Sri Lanka filed under "Indian Ocean". Removed first.</div>

<div class="fix"><b>One label hid two sides.</b> "Air/drone strike" mixes military aircraft and resistance drones. Split by actor.</div>

<div class="fix"><b>A silent software trap.</b> sfdep's EHSA attaches results to the wrong township unless the map is sorted by code. Sorted and checked.</div>
:::

::: {.column width="54%"}
| Step | Question | Method | Compared with |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Task 2** | Where does conflict cluster? Which stand out? | Local Moran's I, Gi\* | 999 shuffles |
| **Task 3** | Where are hot spots emerging or fading? | Mann-Kendall, EHSA, 19 quarters | No trend |
| **Bonus 1** | Do neighbours face the same *kind* of violence? | Multivariate local Geary's c | 999 shuffles |
| **Bonus 2** | Which townships share a conflict timeline? | SKATER on Gi\* paths | Ward, no geography |

: {tbl-colwidths="[13,37,30,20]"}

<div class="small">Each township is compared with its 8 nearest neighbours, as the Lesson 5 notes advise for skewed counts and very uneven township sizes. Only p < 0.05 is mapped. Every result is checked for false alarms and with a second neighbour rule.</div>
:::
:::::

::: notes
The data work was about places and labels. Six rows were not in Myanmar at all. The air strike label mixed both sides of the war. And one sfdep function silently mislabels townships unless the map is sorted, which a check caught. Every statistic is then judged against random shuffling, and every map shows only significant townships.
:::

## Insight 1. One hot block in the Dry Zone, and no lone hot spots

<div class="part">Part 2 · Local spatial association</div>

::::: columns
::: {.column width="60%"}
```{r}
#| fig-width: 8.6
#| fig-height: 7.2
lisa_cols <- c("High-High" = col_high, "Low-Low" = col_low, "High-Low" = col_hl, "Low-High" = col_lh, "Not significant" = col_ns)
gi_cols <- c("Hot spot, p < 0.01" = "#B2400B", "Hot spot, p < 0.05" = "#F1A26B",
             "Cold spot, p < 0.05" = "#8FBCE0", "Cold spot, p < 0.01" = "#0B5A99", "Not significant" = col_ns)
m1 <- tm_shape(lmsa$lisa) +
  tm_polygons(fill = "quadrant", fill.scale = tm_scale_categorical(values = lisa_cols, levels.drop = TRUE),
              fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "Local Moran's I", position = tm_pos_in("left", "bottom"), frame = FALSE),
              col = "white", lwd = 0.15) + states + map_layout + tm_title("Clusters and outliers", size = 1.1, fontface = "bold")
m2 <- tm_shape(lmsa$hcsa) +
  tm_polygons(fill = "spot", fill.scale = tm_scale_categorical(values = gi_cols, levels.drop = TRUE),
              fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "Gi*", position = tm_pos_in("left", "bottom"), frame = FALSE),
              col = "white", lwd = 0.15) + states + map_layout + tm_title("Hot and cold spots", size = 1.1, fontface = "bold")
tmap_arrange(m1, m2, ncol = 2)
```
:::

::: {.column width="40%"}
<div class="statrow">
<div><div class="bignum">`r sum(hq$hot)`</div><div class="bigcap">hot spot townships</div></div>
<div><div class="bignum">`r round(100 * sum(hq$total[hq$hot]) / sum(hq$total))`%</div><div class="bigcap">of all events fall in them</div></div>
</div>

<div class="fix"><b>One core.</b> `r sum(lq$quadrant == "High-High" & lq$ST %in% dz)` of `r sum(lq$quadrant == "High-High")` High-High townships form one block in Sagaing, Magway and Mandalay.</div>

<div class="fix"><b>Cold areas.</b> Yangon, the Ayeyarwady delta and eastern Shan.</div>

<div class="fix"><b>Outliers are quiet edges.</b> No lone hot township. The `r sum(lq$quadrant == "Low-High")` Low-High outliers are calmer places beside the core, such as Nyaung-U.</div>

<div class="small">The High-High core holds after FDR correction and with queen contiguity. Outliers are less stable. Busy Kawkareik is in no cluster, because its neighbours are quiet.</div>
:::
:::::

::: notes
Local Moran's I and Gi star agree. The Dry Zone is one large hot block, and the cold areas are Yangon, the delta and eastern Shan. There is no lone hot township among quiet neighbours. The outliers are calmer townships on the edge of the core, which may be safer pockets or places where events go unreported.
:::

## Insight 2. The core stayed hot, and new hot spots opened around it

<div class="part">Part 3 · Emerging hot spots</div>

::::: columns
::: {.column width="62%"}
```{r}
#| fig-width: 8.8
#| fig-height: 7.2
tm_tot <- ehsa_sf("All armed conflict") %>%
  mutate(hot_band = cut(hot_q, c(-1, 0, 4, 9, 14, 19), labels = c("Never", "1 to 4", "5 to 9", "10 to 14", "15 to 19")))
e1 <- tm_shape(tm_tot) +
  tm_polygons(fill = "shown", fill.scale = tm_scale_categorical(values = ehsa_cols, levels.drop = TRUE),
              fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "Trend, p < 0.05", position = tm_pos_in("left", "bottom"), frame = FALSE),
              col = "white", lwd = 0.15) + states + map_layout + tm_title("Emerging or fading", size = 1.1, fontface = "bold")
e2 <- tm_shape(tm_tot) +
  tm_polygons(fill = "hot_band", fill.scale = tm_scale_categorical(values = c("#F7F2EA", "#FDD0A2", "#FD8D3C", "#D94801", "#7F2704")),
              fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "Quarters as a\nhot spot", position = tm_pos_in("left", "bottom"), frame = FALSE),
              col = "white", lwd = 0.15) + states + map_layout + tm_title("How often hot", size = 1.1, fontface = "bold")
tmap_arrange(e1, e2, ncol = 2)
```
:::

::: {.column width="38%"}
<div class="fix"><b>The core never cooled.</b> Sagaing's core was a hot spot in `r core_q[1]` to `r core_q[2]` of 19 quarters. With no trend, the brief's filter leaves it blank, so the right map shows it.</div>

<div class="fix"><b>New fronts.</b> `r np("Consecutive hotspot")` townships turned hot and stayed hot, in the hills of Bago (East) and on the road to northern Shan.</div>

<div class="fix"><b>Cold to hot.</b> `r np("Oscillating hotspot")` more, across Tanintharyi, Mon, central Rakhine, Bago (East) and the southern Dry Zone.</div>

<div class="fix"><b>Cooling.</b> `r sum(sig_tot$ST == "Yangon" & str_detect(sig_tot$pattern, "coldspot"))` of Yangon's 45 townships, and the northern Shan border after the 2024 ceasefire.</div>
:::
:::::

::: notes
Emerging hot spot analysis maps change, not level. The growing hot spots form a ring around the Dry Zone. The core itself is blank on the trend map because it was hot almost all the time, which the second map makes visible. Yangon cooled steadily, and the northern Shan border went from the hottest place in late 2023 to a cold spot after the ceasefire. The classes were checked against the lecture definitions, and two of sfdep's rules were corrected.
:::

## Insight 3. Each type of violence is moving its own way

<div class="part">Part 3 · Emerging hot spots</div>

::::: columns
::: {.column width="66%"}
```{r}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 6.4
types_sf <- ehsa_sf(c("Battles", "Explosions and remote violence", "Violence against civilians")) %>%
  mutate(variable = factor(variable, levels = c("Battles", "Explosions and remote violence", "Violence against civilians"),
                           labels = c("Battles", "Explosions", "Attacks on civilians")))
tm_shape(types_sf) +
  tm_polygons(fill = "shown", fill.scale = tm_scale_categorical(values = ehsa_cols, levels.drop = TRUE),
              fill.legend = tm_legend_hide(),
              col = "white", lwd = 0.1) +
  tm_facets(by = "variable", ncol = 3) + states +
  tm_layout(bg.color = bg, outer.bg.color = bg, frame = FALSE, panel.label.size = 1.2,
            panel.label.bg.color = bg, panel.label.frame = FALSE, outer.margins = 0,
            legend.bg.color = bg)
```

<div class="small lgd lgd-c lgd-tight">`r html_legend(ehsa_cols, shown_levels(c("Battles", "Explosions and remote violence", "Violence against civilians")))`</div>
:::

::: {.column width="34%"}
<div class="fix"><b>Battles moved south and west.</b> Tanintharyi and central Rakhine turned hot. Northern Shan went cold after the ceasefire.</div>

<div class="fix"><b>Explosions spread to the hills.</b> Bago (East) and Tanintharyi turned hot. Yangon's bombings faded.</div>

<div class="fix"><b>Attacks on civilians moved to the lowlands.</b> `r np("Oscillating hotspot", "Violence against civilians", "Bago (West)")` townships in Bago (West) turned hot, an area of little fighting.</div>
:::
:::::

::: notes
Running the analysis for each type shows three different movements. Ground fighting shifted south and west, to Tanintharyi and central Rakhine. Explosions spread into the hills of Bago East. Attacks on civilians moved into Bago West, a lowland area with little fighting. Battle trends are the weakest, since only about half survive a false discovery rate correction, so that map is a guide rather than a firm result.
:::

## Insight 4. Military air strikes rose `r round(air_x)`-fold and follow the ground war

<div class="part">Part 3 · Emerging hot spots</div>

::::: columns
::: {.column width="52%"}
```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 6
ggplot(charts$remote_mix, aes(year, n, fill = weapon)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.68) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("grey72", col_hl, col_lh, col_low), name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Events") +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2)) +
  theme_slide + theme(legend.position = "top", legend.text = element_text(size = 15),
                      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank())
```

<div class="small">Explosions and remote violence by kind. Military air strikes kept climbing while resistance drone strikes peaked in 2023 and 2024.</div>
:::

::: {.column width="48%"}
::: {.mapleg}
```{r}
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-height: 6.6
tm_shape(ehsa_sf("Military air strikes")) +
  tm_polygons(fill = "shown", fill.scale = tm_scale_categorical(values = ehsa_cols, levels.drop = TRUE),
              fill.legend = tm_legend_hide(),
              col = "white", lwd = 0.15) + states +
  name_box(c("Sagaing", "Magway", "Mandalay", "Rakhine", "Yangon", "Tanintharyi")) +
  map_layout
```

<div class="small lgd lgd-v"><span class="note">Air strike trend,<br>p < 0.05</span> `r html_legend(ehsa_cols, shown_levels("Military air strikes"))`</div>
:::
:::
:::::

::: notes
The military's air strikes grew about 23-fold from 2021 to 2024, and 2025 passed the 2024 total within nine months. Resistance drone strikes, which ACLED files under the same label, peaked in 2023 and 2024 and then fell. The air strike trend map shows townships turning hot across the Dry Zone core and on the new fronts. Air strikes grew most where ground fighting was also growing, which matters for protecting civilians. Central Rakhine is the exception, with few air hot spots.
:::

## Insight 5. When fighting leaves a town, the violence changes kind

<div class="part">Part 4 · Bonus, multivariate local Geary's c</div>

::::: columns
::: {.column width="58%"}
```{r}
#| fig-width: 7.6
#| fig-height: 7.4
geary_cols <- c("All three high" = col_high, "Mostly battles" = col_hl,
                "Few battles, more bombs or attacks on civilians" = "#CC79A7", "All three low" = col_low,
                "Mix unlike its neighbours" = "#000000", "Not significant" = col_ns)
gt_sf <- mmr %>% select(TS_PCODE) %>% left_join(bonus$geary_time, by = "TS_PCODE", relationship = "one-to-many")
tm_shape(gt_sf) +
  tm_polygons(fill = "profile", fill.scale = tm_scale_categorical(values = geary_cols, levels.drop = TRUE),
              fill.legend = tm_legend_hide(),
              col = "white", lwd = 0.1) +
  tm_facets(by = "period", ncol = 2) + states +
  tm_layout(bg.color = bg, outer.bg.color = bg, frame = FALSE, panel.label.size = 1.1,
            panel.label.bg.color = bg, panel.label.frame = FALSE, outer.margins = 0,
            legend.bg.color = bg)
```

<div class="small lgd"><span><i style="color:#CC79A7">■</i> <b>Few battles, more bombs or attacks on civilians</b></span> <span><i style="color:#D55E00">■</i> All three high</span> <span><i style="color:#E69F00">■</i> Mostly battles</span> <span><i style="color:#0072B2">■</i> All three low</span> <span><i style="color:#000000">■</i> Mix unlike its neighbours</span> <span class="note">Significant townships only, p < 0.05</span></div>
:::

::: {.column width="42%"}
<div class="statrow">
<div><div class="bignum">`r nrow(urban)`</div><div class="bigcap">townships share a mix of few battles but many bombs or attacks on civilians</div></div>
<div><div class="bignum" style="color:#6B6B6B">0</div><div class="bigcap">of them sit in a High-High cluster, so count maps call them quiet</div></div>
</div>

<div class="fix"><b>Why Geary's c.</b> Listed in Lesson 5 under other forms of LISA. It compares a township's whole mix of the three types with its neighbours'.</div>

<div class="fix"><b>What changed.</b> Around Mandalay, townships with all three types high in 2021 to 2022 shifted to this mix by 2023 to 2025. Battles left, but bombs and attacks on civilians stayed. In Yangon the mix moved from downtown to the outskirts.</div>

<div class="small">Assumptions. Counts are logged and standardised, and the types weigh the same. Limit. The urban group rests on tens of events per township. It holds with 6 or 10 neighbours.</div>
:::
:::::

::: notes
Local Moran's I looks at one type at a time. Multivariate local Geary's c asks whether neighbours share the same mix of battles, explosions and attacks on civilians. It finds 34 townships, mostly in Yangon and around Mandalay city, with few battles but many bombs and attacks on civilians. Count maps call them quiet. Run on two periods, it shows the pattern spreading around Mandalay as battles moved away. The violence did not stop. It changed kind.
:::

## Key findings and their limits {.findings}

<div class="part">Part 5 · So what</div>

| | Finding | Evidence | Main limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | The Dry Zone is the hot core | `r round(100 * dz_share)`% of events, `r sum(lq$quadrant == "High-High" & lq$ST %in% dz)` of `r sum(lq$quadrant == "High-High")` High-High, hot in `r core_q[1]` to `r core_q[2]` of 19 quarters | Counts, not rates, since no reliable population data exists for 2021 to 2025 |
| **2** | The war widened rather than moved | `r np("Consecutive hotspot")` consecutive and `r np("Oscillating hotspot")` oscillating hot spots ring the core. Conflict regions show the order, core first, south-east and Rakhine later | ACLED records reported events, so places with less access may look calmer |
| **3** | Yangon and northern Shan cooled | `r sum(sig_tot$ST == "Yangon" & str_detect(sig_tot$pattern, "coldspot"))` of 45 Yangon townships in a cold pattern. Northern Shan cold after the 2024 ceasefire | A falling Gi\* means a smaller share of the conflict, not peace |
| **4** | Each type moves its own way | Battles to Rakhine and Tanintharyi, explosions to Bago (East), attacks on civilians to Bago (West) | Battle trends are weak. About half fail the FDR check |
| **5** | Air strikes follow the ground war | About `r round(air_x)`-fold rise, air hot spots in the core and on new fronts | Strikes are counted, not their harm |
| **6** | Violence changes kind when fighting leaves | `r nrow(urban)` townships share a bombs-and-civilians mix, growing around Mandalay | Rests on small counts per township |

: {tbl-colwidths="[4,27,40,29]"}

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
**Core finding.** Where conflict is, where it clusters and where it is growing are three different maps. The core stayed in the Dry Zone while the war widened around it.
:::

::: notes
Each finding comes with its evidence and its main limit. The trend tests also suffer from serial correlation, which the report checks with a corrected Mann-Kendall test. Most trends survive it. Battles are the weakest, with about half failing the false discovery rate check.
:::

:::

::: {.column width="66%"}
<div class="small">SKATER clustering (Lesson 6) groups neighbouring townships whose conflict rose and fell together into eight regions, each needing a different stance.</div>

<div class="act"><b>Sagaing core. Plan long-term support</b><div class="row"><span class="tag">Because</span><span>hot since late 2021, peaking in 2023 and still hot</span></div><div class="row"><span class="tag">Check first</span><span>displacement and access data from UN agencies and local partners</span></div></div>

<div class="act"><b>South-east frontier. Early warning</b><div class="row"><span class="tag">Because</span><span>it rose slowly from 2022 and was at its highest in the last quarter</span></div><div class="row"><span class="tag">Check first</span><span>whether local partners see the same spread, and which roads are open</span></div></div>

<div class="act"><b>Kayah, and Rakhine with the western Dry Zone. Watch for relapse</b><div class="row"><span class="tag">Because</span><span>Kayah peaked in 2022 and 2023, Rakhine in early 2024, and both have eased</span></div><div class="row"><span class="tag">Check first</span><span>whether local ceasefires and front lines still hold</span></div></div>

<div class="act"><b>Across regions. Protect civilians where fighting has moved on</b><div class="row"><span class="tag">Because</span><span>air strikes keep returning to the core and new fronts, and bombs and attacks on civilians stay in Yangon and Mandalay city</span></div><div class="row"><span class="tag">Check first</span><span>casualty records, and under-reporting in tightly controlled cities</span></div></div>

<div class="small">The analysis shows where and when, not why or who is responsible.</div>
:::
:::::

::: notes
SKATER, from Lesson 6, joins neighbouring townships whose quarterly Gi star timelines match into eight conflict regions. Each region calls for a different stance. The Sagaing core needs long-term support. The south-east frontier, still rising, is the early-warning area. Kayah and Rakhine with the western Dry Zone peaked and eased, so they need watching for relapse. And across regions, civilians need protection from air strikes and from the bombs and attacks that stay after battles move on.
:::
